''[[Nerium oleander|Nerium]] obesum'' Forssk. |synonyms_ref = {{GRIN | access-date=30 September 2010}} |subdivision_ranks = Subspecies |subdivision = See text }} '''''Adenium obesum''''', more commonly known as a '''desert rose''', is a [[poisonous]] [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] belonging to the tribe [[Nerieae]] of the subfamily [[Apocynoideae]] of the [[Apocynum|dogbane]] family, [[Apocynaceae]].{{Cite web|last=Schoch|first=C.L.|display-authors=etal|date=2020|title="Adenium obesum", NCBI Taxonomy: a comprehensive update on curation, resources and tools|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?mode=Info&id=69375|url-status=live|access-date=27 August 2021|website=[[National Center for Biotechnology Information]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417021032/https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?mode=Info&id=69375 |archive-date=17 April 2020 }} It is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Sahel]] regions south of the [[Sahara]] (from [[Mauritania]] and [[Senegal]] to [[Sudan]]), tropical and subtropical eastern and southern Africa, as well as the [[Arabian Peninsula]]. Other names for the flower include '''Sabi star''', '''kudu''', '''mock azalea''', and '''impala lily'''. ''Adenium obesum'' is a popular [[houseplant]] and [[bonsai]] in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions. ==Description== {{Unreferenced section|date=July 2022}} It is an [[evergreen]] or drought-deciduous [[Succulent plant|succulent]] [[shrub]] (which can also lose its leaves during cold spells, or according to the subspecies or cultivar). It can grow to {{convert|0.12|–|5|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height, with [[pachycaul]] (disproportionately large) stems and a stout, swollen basal [[caudex]] (a rootstock that protrudes from the soil). The [[leaf|leaves]] are spirally arranged, clustered toward the tips of the shoots, simple entire, leathery in texture, {{convert|5|–|15|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1|–|8|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad. The [[flower]]s are tubular, {{convert|2|–|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long, with the outer portion {{convert|4|–|6|cm|in|abbr=on}} diameter with five petals, resembling those of other related genera such as ''[[Plumeria]]'' and ''[[oleander|Nerium]]''. The flowers tend to be red and pink, often with a whitish blush outward of the throat. ==Taxonomy== {{Unreferenced section|date=July 2022}} Some taxonomies consider some other species in the genus to be subspecies of ''Adenium obesum''. ===Subspecies=== * ''Adenium obesum'' subsp. ''oleifolium'' ([[South Africa]], [[Botswana]]) * ''Adenium obesum'' subsp. ''socotranum'' ([[Socotra]]) * ''Adenium obesum'' subsp. ''somalense'' (Eastern Africa) * ''Adenium obesum'' subsp. ''swazicum'' ([[Eswatini]], South Africa) * ''Adenium obesum'' subsp. ''Arabicum'' ([[Saudi Arabia]], [[Yemen]]) Adenium swazicum is a critically endangered African species native to Eswatini and Mozambique, growing up to {{convert|0.7|m}} tall. Adenium somalense is also native to Africa, inhabiting Tanzania, Kenya, and Somalia, and reaching heights of {{convert|5|m}}, which makes it the largest of these four subspecies. Adenium socotranum is native exclusively to the island of Socotra, and can grow to be {{convert|4.6|m}}, but despite its small range, it is of least concern regarding endangerment. It can swell up to {{convert|8|ft}} in diameter at the base.{{cite web|author=Siby Xavier |date=23 October 2024 |language=en |title=Meet the Majestic Adenium Socotranum: Socotra's Floral Gem |url=https://socotrabooking.com/meet-the-majestic-adenium-socotranum-socotras-floral-gem/}} Adenium oleifolium is near threatened in the wild and is the smallest of these subspecies, growing at the tallest to {{convert|0.4|m}}. [[Adenium Arabicum]] a species is a monoecious and self-sterile, common names include desert rose, elephant's foot, and Adan bush, arabicum is native to Saudi Arabia and Yemen. ==Ecology== Caterpillars of the polka-dot wasp moth (''[[Syntomeida epilais]]'') are known to feed on the desert rose, along with feeding on [[oleander]]s.{{cite web|title=Oleander caterpillar (Syntomeida epilais)|url=http://trec.ifas.ufl.edu/mannion/pdfs/OleanderCaterpillar.pdf|website=UF/IFAS|access-date=26 March 2018|date=August 2006|archive-date=11 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151211130256/http://trec.ifas.ufl.edu/mannion/pdfs/OleanderCaterpillar.pdf}} In areas with year-round warm weather, they can bloom throughout the year.{{Cite web |title=Is Adenium Obesum Poisonous to Dogs? |url=https://homeguides.sfgate.com/adenium-obesum-poisonous-dogs-76694.html |access-date=14 May 2022 |department=Home Guides |website=[[SFGate]] |language=en}} ==Uses== ''Adenium obesum'' produces a sap in its roots and stems that contains [[cardiac glycoside]]s. This sap is used as [[arrow poison]] for hunting large game throughout much of Africa{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7FJqgQ3_tnUC |first=G.H. |last=Schmelzer |first2=A. |last2=Gurib-Fakim |title=Medicinal Plants |year=2008 |publisher=Plant Resources of Tropical Africa |isbn=978-90-5782-204-9 |pages=46–49}} and as a [[fish toxins|fish toxin]].John 'Lofty' Wiseman ''SAS Survival Handbook, Revised Edition'' p. 240; William Morrow Paperbacks (2009) {{ISBN|978-1875900060}} ==Cultivation== [[File:Adenium obesum at the campus of Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute in Belur Math, Howrah.jpg|thumb|Flowers of Adenium obesum in [[West Bengal]], India.]] ''Adenium obesum'' is a popular [[houseplant]] and [[bonsai]]{{cite web |last=D'Cruz |first=Mark |title=Ma-Ke Bonsai Care Guide for Adenium obesum |url=http://guide.makebonsai.com/bonsai_species_guide_training.asp?SpeciesID=5111&Name=Adenium_obesum |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121214051529/http://guide.makebonsai.com/bonsai_species_guide_training.asp?SpeciesID=5111&Name=Adenium_obesum |archive-date=14 December 2012 |access-date=11 May 2011 |website=Ma-Ke Bonsai}} in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions. It requires a sunny location and a minimum indoor temperature in winter of {{convert|10|C|F|abbr=on}}. It thrives on a [[Xeriscaping|xeric]] watering regime as required by [[Cactus|cacti]]. ''A. obesum'' is typically propagated by seed or stem cuttings. The numerous hybrids are propagated mainly by grafting on to seedling rootstock. While plants grown from seed are more likely to have the swollen caudex at a young age, with time many cutting-grown plants cannot be distinguished from seed-grown plants. Like many plants, ''Adenium obesum'' can also be propagated [[in vitro]] using [[plant tissue culture]].{{cite journal |last1=Kanchanapoom |first1=Kantamaht |last2=Sunheem |first2=Sunisa |last3=Kanchanapoom |first3=Kamnoon |date=5 December 2010 |title=In vitro Propagation of Adenium obesum (Forssk.) Roem. and Schult. |url=http://www.notulaebotanicae.ro/index.php/nbha/article/view/4604/5093 |journal=Notulae Botanicae Horti Agrobotanici Cluj-Napoca |language=en |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=209–213 |doi=10.15835/nbha3834604 |issn=1842-4309 |access-date=26 January 2016 |doi-access=free}} This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web |title=Adenium obesum |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/426/Adenium-obesum/Details |access-date=23 February 2020 |website=RHS Plant Selector}} ==Symbolic and cultural references== The species has been depicted on [[postage stamps]] issued by various countries.{{cite web|title=Adenium obesum|url=http://stampdata.com/thing.php?id=11212|website=StampData|access-date=24 March 2020}} ==See also== * [[List of poisonous plants]] * ''[[Pachypodium]]'' - another [[caudiciform]] member of the Apocynaceae ==Gallery== File:Bottle Trees, Socotra Island (9888518324).jpg|Close-up of stand of ''A. obesum var. socotranum'', [[Socotra]] File:Desert Rose, Socotra Is (17131661372).jpg|''A. obesum var. socotranum'', trunk of single extreme [[pachycaul]] specimen, Socotra File:Desert rose Adenium obesum in Tanzania 2259 Nevit.jpg|Group of plants growing in scrubland, Tanzania File:Adenium obesum - Marie Selby Botanical Gardens - Sarasota, Florida - DSC01083.jpg|Cultivated [[bonsai]] specimen with picturesquely contorted [[caudex]] and roots, Florida File:RCN Mother.jpg|Cultivated specimen in Thailand flowering profusely.
